item.title: How old power absorbs reform
item.description: ON SEPTEMBER 6, Bangladesh’s Parliament passed the Prevention and Remedy of Enforced Disappearance Bill, 2026, and the National Human Rights Commission Bill, 2026. Read in isolation, both laws appear to mark an important departure from the recent past. Enforced disappearance, one of the most painful symbols of the previous political order, has finally been recognised through a dedicated legal framework, while the National Human Rights Commission, long criticised for its limited......

item.title: The kind of society that makes pluralism possible
item.description: THE recent controversy in Brahmanbaria is more than a dispute between a lawmaker and a group of Qawmi students. It is a small but revealing episode in Bangladesh’s larger struggle over religion, culture, and public life. Cumilla lawmaker and National Citizens Party leader Hasnat Abdullah’s final response was conciliatory. item.title: The politics of the past: who controls history?
item.description: THE nexus between history, power and politics has become increasingly evident in the contemporary world, driven by political shifts and the aggressive instrumentalisation of the past to legitimise state authority. Demagogues, fascists and tyrants routinely weaponise historical narrative to serve their political ends.
